---
title: "Session 11 guided lab"
subtitle: "Four short exercises: conditions and functions"
---

## Start here

Work in **BIOS6301-mywork.Rproj**. Copy either
[the Quarto starter](starter/functions-lab.qmd) or
[the R Markdown starter](starter/functions-lab.Rmd) to `work/session11/` in
your personal repository. Use just one format.

The starter runs as supplied. Complete the clearly marked TODOs, then Render
or Knit again. All data are small synthetic vectors included in the file;
the exercises use only base R and the standard `stats` package.
Keep your functions in this report. No extra helper files or data downloads
are required.

## 1. Choose a condition

**Lecture connection:** one decision with `if`; one label per value with `ifelse()`.

- Run the supplied length check for four baseline readings and two follow-up
  readings. Explain why it avoids a misleading subtraction.
- Replace `followup` with `c(138, 132, 150, 155)` and rerun the same check.
  You should obtain changes `-12, -8, -10, 0`. The rows are already matched by
  participant; equal lengths alone cannot establish that match.
- For `change <- c(-2, NA, 1, 0)`, replace the placeholder labels with nested
  `ifelse()` calls. Return `"decrease"`, `"missing"`, `"no decrease"`, and
  `"no decrease"`. Keep the supplied `any()` decision and explain why
  `if (change < 0)` would not work.

The `any()` example asks only whether an observed decrease exists; it does
not treat missing observations as known non-decreases.

## 2. Write and call a small function

**Lecture connection:** help pages, parameters, defaults, return values, and explicit inputs.

Open `help("median", package = "stats")` in the Console. For the supplied call
`stats::median(c(10, NA, 14), na.rm = TRUE)`, identify the package, function,
the default for `na.rm`, and the supplied argument that overrides it.
Use **Value** to predict the return value and its length, then run the call.

Complete `centre_values(x, centre = 0)` by replacing its placeholder body
with `x - centre`. Run the two supplied calls and save their results:

- Default center: `c(10, NA, 14)`.
- `centre = 12`: `c(-2, NA, 2)`.

In one sentence, explain why passing the center as an argument is preferable
to reading a global `reference_mean` inside the function.

## 3. Read a function with checks

**Lecture connection:** validation and early returns.

The complete `safe_mean()` is supplied. Run its four example calls; do not
rewrite it. Explain which branch handles each input:

| Input | Expected result |
|---|---|
| `c(2, NA, 4)` | `3` |
| `numeric(0)` | Numeric `NA` |
| `c(NA_real_, NA_real_)` | Numeric `NA` |
| `"4"` | An error about numeric input |

The last call is wrapped in `try(..., silent = TRUE)` so the expected error
can be shown without stopping the report. Missing measurements are allowed;
character values are invalid input.

## 4. Reuse the function and check the result

**Lecture connection:** quoted column names and refactoring repeated code.

The starter calculates two observed means using repeated code. Replace the
two placeholder assignments with calls to `safe_mean()`, extracting each
column with `markers[["column_name"]]`. Keep the original results for comparison.

Run the supplied `isTRUE(all.equal(...))` comparisons. Both should be `TRUE`;
the means should be approximately `5.1` and `10.5`. Explain in one sentence
what these comparisons tell you about the refactor.

## Submit

Submit your completed `.qmd` or `.Rmd` file and its rendered HTML, including
the short explanations above. Restart R and render the saved file once to
check that it works without objects left in the Console.

The lecture's paired-change helpers and separate R scripts remain reference
examples. Sessions 12 and 13 supply the helpers needed for their own labs.
